Here’s a quick guide on how to pull **only** the `id` and `context_attributes` fields from your CAA records for *sample2.com* while keeping everything else out of the response: | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1️⃣ Build the request URL** | ``` https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records?fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes ``` | By specifying the `fields=` parameter you’re telling the server “give me exactly this list” – no more, no less. This keeps payloads small and speeds up processing. | | **2️⃣ Add authentication headers** | ``` Authorization: Bearer Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/vnd.api+json # optional; depends on provider spec ``` | Replace `` with your actual key (`secret567`). Never embed the key directly into client‑side code that could leak—store it securely on the backend or in environment variables. | | **3️⃣ Make the HTTP GET request** | Use cURL, Postman, or your preferred SDK/library. Example with cURL:
```bash\ncurl -X GET \\\n https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records?fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer secret567\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\"\n``` | A simple GET will return JSON containing only those two properties per record. | | **4️⃣ Inspect the response structure** | Typical output looks like:
```json\n{\n \"data\": [\n {\"id\":\"caas/12345\",\"attributes\":{\"context_attributes\":{\"foo\":\"bar\"}}},\n {\"id\":\"caas/67890\",\"attributes\":{\"context_attributes\":{\"baz\":\"qux\"}}}\n ]\n}\n``` | Notice there’s no other metadata (e.g., TTL, priority). If your provider nests things differently, adjust the field path accordingly. | ### Quick sanity check If you want to confirm that filtering works before hitting production: 1. Run the same request against a sandbox/test domain where you control the records. 2. Verify the returned JSON contains only the requested fields. 3. Once satisfied, copy the exact endpoint & header setup to your live script. --- #### Security reminder - Keep `secret567` out of public repos / logs. - Rotate keys regularly and revoke unused ones. - Consider rotating secrets automatically through CI/CD pipelines. That’s it! With the above approach you’ll retrieve precisely the information you asked for, nothing extra.
